paper_title: How to Reduce Charge Recombination in Organic Solar Cells: There are Still Lessons to Learn from P3HT:PCBM

knowledge_points.content: DCB-processed P3HT:PCBM solar cells maintain high performance at active layer thicknesses exceeding 300 nm, whereas CB-processed devices show a drop to 1.1% PCE at 350 nm due to voltage-dependent photocurrent.
knowledge_points.evidence: Clearly, only the slow grown DCB devices maintain (and even improve) their performance by increasing L from around 50 to over 300 nm. In contrast, for the CB devices... the thickest CB device (L = 350 nm) achieves an efficiency of only 1.1%

knowledge_points.content: The use of 1,2-dichlorobenzene (DCB) as a solvent facilitates a slow drying rate that allows P3HT to form aggregates of high crystalline quality, which thermal annealing alone cannot achieve in rapidly dried chlorobenzene (CB) films.
knowledge_points.evidence: We hypothesize that the fast evaporation of CB gives the P3HT not enough time to organize into larger aggregates, and that thermal annealing cannot fully convert the disordered structure into a highly ordered one with an extended conjugation.

knowledge_points.content: Using the Spano model for H-aggregates, the intramolecular free exciton bandwidth (W) was determined to be 87 meV for DCB-processed blends compared to 132 meV for CB-processed blends, indicating higher molecular order in DCB films.
knowledge_points.evidence: Table 1 and the dashed lines in Figure 4 show the results of the Spano analysis... W [meV]: CB (132), DCB (87).

knowledge_points.content: The conjugation length of P3HT in DCB-processed blends is estimated at approximately 40 repeat units, significantly higher than the 27 repeat units found in CB-processed blends.
knowledge_points.evidence: We can estimate the conjugation length using previous approaches, which gives about 27 repeat units for the CB blends and 40 repeat units for the DCB blends.

knowledge_points.content: Electron tomography reveals that DCB-processed P3HT:PCBM blends possess a finer phase separation (average domain size d ≈ 5.9 nm) compared to CB-processed blends (d ≈ 9.6 nm).
knowledge_points.evidence: While the CB sample exhibits well-separated and homogeneously distributed domains in the order of 10 nm, the DCB sample shows a much finer phase separation... average of d = 5.9 ± 0.4 nm [for DCB] and d = 9.6 ± 0.2 nm [for CB].

knowledge_points.content: DCB-processed blends exhibit a higher phase purity than CB-processed blends, with an estimated mixed phase volume fraction of 26% compared to 31%.
knowledge_points.evidence: This way we arrive at about 31% mixed phase in the CB blends and 26% in the DCB blends... the DCB blends also exhibit a higher overall phase purity.

knowledge_points.content: Hole mobilities in both CB and DCB-processed P3HT:PCBM blends are approximately 1.3-1.6 x 10^-8 m^2 V^-1 s^-1, indicating that macroscopic transport is not the primary cause of the performance difference.
knowledge_points.evidence: Table 2 lists the resulting electron and hole mobilities. As the most important result, the magnitude of both μn and μp appears to be fairly independent of the solvent used.

knowledge_points.content: The bimolecular recombination rate constant (k2) in optimized DCB-processed P3HT:PCBM is approximately 1 x 10^-19 m^3 s^-1, which is roughly 20 times lower than in CB-processed blends.
knowledge_points.evidence: we estimate that k2 must be about 1 × 10^−19 m^3 s^−1 or less... confirming that the key difference between the CB and DCB devices lies in the free charge recombination, which is about 20 times more reduced in the DCB blends.

knowledge_points.content: The hole diffusion length (LD) in optimized DCB-processed P3HT:PCBM devices is estimated to be at least 140 nm, facilitating efficient collection in thick-junction devices.
knowledge_points.evidence: The fact that charges are collected from a 300-nm device without notice-able loss means that the hole diffusion length must be at least around 140 nm.

knowledge_points.content: High-quality aggregates support charge delocalization, which increases the dissociation rate (kd) of interfacial charge-transfer (CT) states formed during carrier encounters, thereby reducing the net recombination rate.
knowledge_points.evidence: The high-quality aggregates support charge delocalization, which assists the re-dissociation of interfacial charge-transfer states formed upon the encounter of free carriers.

knowledge_points.content: Optimized DCB-processed P3HT:PCBM devices function as Shockley-type solar cells even in thick junctions, characterized by a competition parameter α < 1.
knowledge_points.evidence: An important finding from Figure 6b is that under nearly all conditions tested, the DCB devices operate as Shockley-type solar cells (α < 1). This is an outstanding result for OPVs, especially with thick active layers.

knowledge_points.content: Phase separation and domain size are found to be of secondary importance to molecular order and crystalline quality in determining the strength of bimolecular recombination in P3HT:PCBM blends.
knowledge_points.evidence: In contrast, the encounter rate and the size of the phase-separated domains appear to be less important... optimization of the domain size, for example through nanostructuring, is not a promising approach to significantly suppress recombination.
